errors.text_span: This pie chart visualizes the distribution of quantifiers and operations across four reasoning categories.
errors.evidence: The figure contains three separate and distinct pie charts, but the description incorrectly describes them as a single pie chart.
The three charts contain 4, 3, and 2 slices respectively, for a total of 9 slices, not 10.
There is no slice labeled "Quantifiers". The slices with the value 27.91% are "Limiter" (which is pink) and "Negation" (which is orange).
The "Limiter" slice is colored pink in the chart, not orange. The orange slice is "Negation".
The "Negation" slice is colored orange in the chart, not yellow.
The full label for this slice is "Absolute Absence", and its color is light purple, not yellow.
This slice does not exist in the chart. The model appears to have split the "Absolute Absence" label into two separate, hallucinated slices, which also contributes to the incorrect total slice count.
The color of the "Approximate Quantities" slice is light yellow/beige, not green.
"Disjunctive & Conjunctive" is the title of the third pie chart, not a slice label. The description fails to mention the actual slices "Disjunctive" (49.51%) and "Conjunctive" (50.49%).
